transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-26
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Denise Cruz (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Procurement), Priya Desai (Aurora Legal), Evan Kim (Aurora CTO), Jordan Lee (Aurora Sec), Marta Ruiz (Aurora DevOps)

Summary: quick run-through of MSA/DPA, SLAs, onboarding timelines; collect action items.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. quick intro, i'm maya from redwood, i'm joined by samir on the technical side and denise who will help with onboarding and CSM stuff.
[00:14] Liam: thanks maya, liam here, we'll keep procurement side notes; priya's our counsel, evan is our cto, jordan on security and marta ops.
[00:25] Maya: great. objective today is to walk through the MSA/DPA redlines you've sent, go over SLAs and clarify dedicated vs hosted for the pilot and trucking the timeline to procurement approvals.
[00:40] Priya: yes, we sent initial redline earlier this week, biggest items are data residency language, breach notification timing and indemnity caps. also curious what evidence you can provide on SOC 2, pen tests, and any attestation for cloud regions.
[00:58] Samir: totally. we can share our SOC 2 report and latest pen test summary — i'll drop links after the call. for data residency, we support region pinning on Dedicated and Private — so you can keep data in eu-west or us-east, depending on the plan.
[01:20] Jordan: when you say private, you mean vpc and on-prem, right? we've got an on-prem air-gapped requirement for one workload.
[01:28] Samir: right — Redwood Private offers customer-managed networking and an on-prem package for regulated workloads. small caveat: the on-prem option is a separate agreement and involves a packaging lead time.
[01:41] Evan: what's the lead time? ballpark.
[01:44] Samir: typical on-prem is 6-10 weeks from contract + scoping, but we can do a hybrid where we run Dedicated in your cloud region with VPC peering to satisfy the residency faster.
[01:58] Priya: also, SLA credits: your MSA states 99.9 availability for hosted and 99.95 for dedicated — can we get clarity on measurement windows and credit calculation? the redline asks for 1% credits per cumulative hour beyond threshold.
[02:18] Maya: yes, so our SLA table defines availability per billing month; downtime minutes are measured using service health metrics, and credits are a percentage of monthly invoice. we can share the SLA matrix; samir will follow up with the exact calc and examples.
[02:36] Liam: procurement note — our finance needs a maximum cap on aggregate credits, and we need to know indemnity exposures.
[02:45] Maya: indemnity caps are negotiable; typically we propose liability limited to fees paid in prior 12 months, but we can discuss incremental exceptions for data breaches.
[02:58] Priya: that sounds standard. for breach notification we asked for 72 hours. is that doable?
[03:05] Jordan: we generally like 48 but understand 72 is common.
[03:08] Samir: operationally we aim to notify customers within 48 hours for confirmed incidents, but legal language often lands at 72 to allow for triage. we can commit to 48 for priority incidents — we'll flag that in the redline.
[03:26] Priya: great. can you also confirm encryption at rest key management? we use AWS KMS and would prefer a customer-managed key option.
[03:36] Samir: yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM for Private. for Hosted we have options for Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) via our KMS integration — i'll include the integration notes and limitations.
[03:51] Marta: on the networking side, if we do Dedicated in our aws acct, what does peering look like? do you support direct connect or vpn only?
[03:59] Samir: we support both VPN and Direct Connect; Dedicated typically lives in our managed account but can be deployed into a customer VPC for enterprise plans. for hybrid we recommend direct connect for predictable latency.
[04:14] Evan: for the pilot we want to run a 4-week bench with our conversational agent — what are the perf numbers for a medium model at 2k tokens? both latency p95 and throughput targets.
[04:25] Samir: i'll pull Dedicated throughput numbers; rough estimate for a gpus-type node is p95 ~220-260ms per token at 2k depending on quantization; we can run a benchmark in your environment. we'll also share a perf spreadsheet we've been using (link).
[04:44] Liam: good. procurement will want pricing approvals — do you have an enterprise pricing sheet and any standard discount for reserved capacity?
[04:52] Maya: yes, for Dedicated we have reserved capacity pricing with 12/24 month commit discounts. i'll attach the pricing sheet; we can provide a pricing addendum for the MSA.
[05:05] Priya: back to DPA — we need data deletion clauses for user data and logs. how long do you retain request logs by default?
[05:13] Samir: default retention is 90 days, can be extended or reduced depending on plan. logs used for debugging are kept 90 days; we can add shorter retention for sensitive workloads — we'll note that in the DPA redline.
[05:27] Priya: will redwood provide audit logs and ability to export them? for compliance we need access to request traces and erasure proofs.
[05:35] Denise: yes, audit logs can be exported and we have a tracing hook; for Dedicated customers we provide more granular token-level logs and longer retention as an add-on.
[05:45] Jordan: any caveats about structured output or tool-calling features and sending callbacks? need to ensure callbacks don't leak into shared caches.
[05:55] Samir: good call — caching policies are configurable; we have KV cache/prefix cache options and those are disabled by default for private data. sometimes transcription shows K-V cash in logs — sorry, that's a bad ASR — but yes, caches are controllable.
[06:12] Liam: procurement question — what do you need from us to move legal forward? we already sent a few redlines.
[06:18] Maya: best path is we send a consolidated redline that combines your comments with our standard language. we'll include a cover sheet highlighting changes and rationale. then priya can respond with any remaining open items.
[06:29] Priya: do you have a suggested timeline? procurement would like signed docs within 4-6 weeks if possible.
[06:35] Maya: doable, assuming a single round of redlines. if multiple heavy legal rounds it can stretch. we'll aim for initial redline back by 4/30.
[06:45] Evan: onboarding — what does the pilot onboarding look like and who from redwood will be assigned?
[06:51] Denise: i'll be the CSM and will run the onboarding checklist. typical pilot has: kickoff, environment setup, test dataset ingestion, benchmark run, and a final review. total ~2-4 weeks depending on the customer's readiness.
[07:06] Marta: network windows — we may need scheduled maintenance windows for peering setup, can we do that with your infra team?
[07:12] Samir: yes, we'll coordinate. for Dedicated deployments we do a joint runbook and have a ticket channel for network ops.
[07:21] Liam: procurement also flagged insurance — minimum cyber liability. what are typical limits you carry?
[07:27] Maya: standard is $5M cyber liability; we can provide certificate of insurance. if you need higher we can discuss.
[07:35] Priya: indemnity and liability — need clarifications on exclusions for third-party claims.
[07:40] Maya: we'll ask legal to flag the few exceptions and propose a clean exhibit for IP and third-party claims; that's often a short negotiation.
[07:49] Jordan: on SOC2 we saw the summary — can you confirm the scope covers production infra and change management?
[07:56] Samir: yes, scope covers production and core change mgmt; i'll include the SOC2 type II report and scope page in the pack.
[08:05] Liam: good. two procurement asks: 1) an MSA signature copy w/ fully executed exhibit for pricing, 2) DPA redline back.
[08:14] Maya: we'll deliver both.
[08:16] Priya: one more on data residency — if we route EU traffic to eu-west, are backups replicated outside region by default?
[08:24] Samir: backups can be region-restricted for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has geo-replication for resilience by default but we can opt-out and pin backups to region for enterprise customers. we'll outline exact behavior in the DPA.
[08:40] Evan: about SLA measurement — if we have partial region outage, does SLA apply per-region or global?
[08:48] Samir: the SLA is typically per-service and per-region; we'll include language to clarify regional measurements and fallback policies.
[09:00] Marta: our security team wants to run a short pen-test window post-onboarding. is that allowed?
[09:07] Maya: yes, we permit coordinated vulnerability testing per our security testing policy; we'll provide the process and point of contact.
[09:16] Priya: redline concern on export controls and gov data — we need covenant that PII and regulated data is not processed outside allowed jurisdictions.
[09:27] Samir: we'll add jurisdictional restrictions for specific datasets under the DPA and the Private offering.
[09:36] Liam: procurement timeline reminder — finance needs the final pricing and bill run schedule to approve the PO.
[09:44] Maya: i'll include a pricing addendum that shows monthly billing cadence and any commit discounts.
[09:50] Evan: any dependencies from our side to start the pilot? creds, network, sso?
[09:55] Denise: minimal: service account to access log exports, a network window for peering/direct connect, and SSO setup if you want admin SSO. we'll share an onboarding checklist.
[10:06] Priya: question about eDiscovery and legal hold — how do you handle requests to preserve logs?
[10:12] Samir: we keep immutable snapshots for legal hold on request; we'll add an exhibit describing preservation process and cost.
[10:22] Liam: procurement also asked about termination assistance and data return timelines. current redline asks for 30 days to export data.
[10:30] Maya: we typically provide 30 days export assistance and then delete per the DPA. we can extend that window as a contract exhibit.
[10:40] Priya: outstanding is the indemnity carveout for open-source code used in model stacks. do you accept standard disclaimers?
[10:47] Samir: we carve out open-source components; liability is limited there. we'll include a third-party software schedule.
[10:55] Liam: ok, sounds good. any blockers on your side?
[11:00] Maya: no blockers; main items are redline consolidation, SOC2/pen test docs, and the SLA matrix. samir will handle the technical artifacts.
[11:09] Samir: i'll share the perf spreadsheet and dedicated SLA table; i'll also include notes about kv cache behavior and quantization tradeoffs — apologies if ASR earlier said 'K-V cash' — that's the speech model acting up.
[11:23] Priya: can we get a short clause on data subject requests and erasure timelines? current legal pos is 30 days.
[11:30] Samir: yes we support 30-day DSARs; will include the operational steps.
[11:38] Denise: next steps recap: maya sends consolidated redline + security pack by 4/30; samir sends SLA/perf docs by 4/29; priya to reply with open items by 5/7; we'll set follow-up onboarding call week of 5/11.
[11:55] Liam: noted. procurement will queue the PO after pricing addendum and bank approvals.
[12:03] Evan: small question — for the pilot, does the hosted plan allow us to run in dedicated region with strict retention?
[12:11] Samir: hosted can be region-pinned but some artifacts (backups) default geo-replicate; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[12:22] Priya: legal will look at the redline and we may request a quick legal-to-legal call if anything material comes up.
[12:29] Maya: fine. we are open to a legal call.
[12:33] Liam: thanks everyone, that covers it.
[12:36] Maya: thanks all. follow up email with links and action items coming in next 24 hours.
[12:43] (meeting ends)

References shared: pricing addendum (link: https://redwood.example.com/pricing/enterprise-addendum), SLA matrix (internal link), SOC2 and pen test pack (link to doc repo), MSA draft (link: https://redwood.example.com/legal/msa-draft.pdf).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and ASR typos (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache).
